security_boundary.note: The change tightens the host / build-environment boundary and loosens nothing. Read against the code: resolveRuntime is the only reader of Runtime.CLI outside tests; what it returns is containerRuntimes' own string or detection's, never the configured one; its three callers (newDriver, runClean, doctor) return its error before anything is looked up, run or created; and the value is printed once, with %q. The design's Security note states the threat, the change and the five residuals accurately (a repository still chooses among the three runtimes and the driver; PATH is the user's; F1 to F4 and F9 are project-config-trust's). The design review r1 records the note as acknowledged; the merge acknowledges it (FLOW-08). TEST-08 runs for the release that carries this.

findings.finding: TestDoctorIgnoresAnUnusedRuntime runs the real `warden doctor` of each VM driver in a child process with HOME and USERPROFILE moved, but not the user cache directory. firecracker's doctor is not read-only: its reflink probe creates <user cache>/warden/firecracker/work, writes and removes probe files there and runs `cp --reflink=always`, beside other host commands (`systemctl is-active firewalld` when not root). On Linux with XDG_CACHE_HOME set in the caller's environment `make test` therefore creates that directory in the developer's real cache and leaves it; by the same code it does on Windows, under LocalAppData (not run here). Reproduced here: XDG_CACHE_HOME=<scratch> go test ./cmd/warden -run TestDoctorIgnoresAnUnusedRuntime leaves <scratch>/warden/firecracker/work. With XDG_CACHE_HOME unset (this host, and the CI runner by default) the cache is under the moved HOME and nothing is left. The test's result does not depend on any of this. Plan note B's 'doctor is read-only under every driver' is the premise that does not hold. The clean rows of TestUnusedRuntimeIsNotValidated (line 512) do redirect XDG_CACHE_HOME and LocalAppData.
findings.suggestion: In the doctor rows, set XDG_CACHE_HOME and LocalAppData to t.TempDir() before the child starts, as the clean rows do (two lines; child.Env is built from os.Environ() afterwards). Correct note B's sentence at Consolidation.

findings.finding: Test 3's build is the one tier-1 proof that a supported runtime named by a project's warden.toml is still built with (task 16). It runs warden with the caller's environment. Where WARDEN_CTR_CLI is set (the design notes that the native launcher's allowlist admits it), the variable outranks the file, the build never reads the file's value, and the script still prints 'built with cli = ... in the project's warden.toml'. Test 0's rt_warden removes WARDEN_CTR_CLI and WARDEN_DRIVER for this reason; Test 3 does not. On the CI runner neither variable is set, so the case is sound there.
findings.suggestion: Run that build, and the doctor call that picks NAMED_RUNTIME (line 284), under `env -u WARDEN_CTR_CLI -u WARDEN_DRIVER`.

informational.topic: For the human's eye: the message a hostile repository's file gets
informational.note: With cli = "./tools/docker" in a cloned repository's warden.toml, the error is the transitional one: 'the container runtime is named, not given as a path' and 'To fix: set it to docker; warden looks docker up on PATH, so if it is installed outside PATH, add its directory to PATH'. That is the design's wording (The error, Transitional), no directory from the value is printed, and the tests pin it. Unlike the permanent error for a file, it does not end with '--runtime with one of those replaces it for one command', the way to build someone else's repository without editing it; the configuration reference does say so. Not a finding: the design's table gives each transitional form a fix of its own and the review approved it. If the clause is wanted on the file-sourced transitional messages too, that is a wording change for Design.

TestDoctorIgnoresAnUnusedRuntime's hyperv row runs doctor's Hyper-V host probes (PowerShell) on a Windows host, so its duration there depends on the host; not run here. CI does not run make test on Windows; the tracked gap runtime-cli-project-path-windows runs go test ./cmd/warden there and will show it.
